narrative: Material PL2__ME3E7FF6 exhibits smooth demand with normal distribution (CV=0.43) and moderate lead time variability (CV=0.99). The optimized (r,Q) policy increases safety stock to 1,111 units and sets order quantity to 5,333 units (capacity-constrained from EOQ of 13,474), achieving a 95% service level while reducing total annual costs by $14,468 (88.5%). Lead time variability is the dominant factor affecting buffer requirements, contributing 83.5% of total variance.
warnings: EOQ (13,474 units) exceeds storage capacity when combined with safety stock; order quantity hard-capped at 5,333 units (= floor(6444.659 - 1111)). Capacity constraint is binding — storage expansion would further reduce ordering costs.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth near-normal demand with moderate lead-time variability makes the continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal: the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty and the fixed EOQ-derived order quantity minimises total ordering and holding costs subject to MOQ and storage constraints.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds at 6,444 units; the unconstrained EOQ is 13,474 units. Capping Q to 5,333 units increases annual ordering cost from the unconstrained optimum but still delivers 88.5% savings vs. the SAP baseline. Expanding storage to ~15,000 units would unlock the full EOQ benefit.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (504) + safety stock (1,111) = 1,615 < max_storage_units (6,444); no MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
